summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube dependence presented with a 4-day history of right-sided/epigastric/suprapubic abdominal pain and baseline nausea without vomiting. She was admitted to the surgery service, made NPO with IV fluids and tube feeds held initially; CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast showed no small bowel obstruction and stable G-tube position. Her pain and nausea were controlled with supportive care, tube feeds were restarted and gradually advanced to her baseline goal of 60 mL/hr, and she received daily wound packing and dressing changes for her midline incision. She was discharged home ambulatory and alert with home services for wound care and medications including rifaximin, lansoprazole, sucralfate, docusate, and PRN hydromorphone, along with return precautions for fever, worsening pain, vomiting, bloating, or concerning wound drainage.
